items.title: Arthur "Monk" Hazel Interview, 1959-07-16
items.q: I played the blues with Martha Boswell playing the organ. You know these little church organs, like little home organs like that. We played the blues. She playing the organ and me playing the cornet.

ctx.x: I was gonna ask first of all, just how old you were when you started with the drums? Had you played anything else at all first? That was a very good thing.

No, no, that was, that was, on account of my dad being there. Yeah. He bought me, first he bought me a snare drum. You see? Mm-hmm. And then I just, just played the snare drum. Like I told you, every time they'd come running for Rag Baby, well I'd have to take his place. And then, and then the parades. You had your own snare drum then you got. My dad bought me a snare drum. Incidentally, later on he hocked it. And, and I went to, there was a place down here on, down around Napoleon Avenue called the Mysterious…
Well, they didn't live across the river then. No. Well, I thought maybe they were from over there. They never did live across, no, the Hardys lived across the river, you see.

items.q: Emmett's sister and the Boswell kids were, were, were real friendly. And that's how, how, how Emmett happened to go to the Boswell's house, through his sister.

ctx.x: Well, they didn't live across the river then. No. Well, I thought maybe they were from over there. They never did live across, no, the Hardys lived across the river, you see.

I mean, they Hardys probably all did. And, and, and, and Emmett's sister and the Boswell kids were, were, were real friendly. And that's how, how, how Emmett happened to go to the Boswell's house, through his sister. And they had a, they had a, a little trio. They played, they played both. When they played classical, Connie would play the cello, Martha would play the piano, and Vett would play the violin. And when they played jazz, Vett would play the banjo, Connie, uh, Martha would play the piano. And, uh, and,…
